properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25, correcting the evidence base and supplying the doctrine. Nothing here is planned and #334 stands.

═══ HIS METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION, WHICH IS RIGHT AND MATTERS ═══

*"most of these are after the fact. meaning, they were developed before reflow2 really started defining rungs. they might have been done differently if reflow2 defined rungs when these designs were first started."*

**THE SAMPLE IS CONTAMINATED.** Every design measured — flo2, qbench, dynograph-foundation, dev_storyflow, mapwright, music_graph, reflow2's own — was built while reflow2 offered no ladder concept, no instruction mentioning `level`, and no detector for depth. They are evidence of what happens with NO GUIDANCE, not evidence of what a guided user would produce. Any conclusion of the form "users only go two rungs deep, so depth does not matter" is unsupported, and one was drawn from them earlier today and is withdrawn here.

*"maybe better to use real world examples or case studies than our own, which were all done prior to a complete reflow2."*

═══ THE DOCTRINE HE SUPPLIED — LAYERS ARE SET UPFRONT, BY RULE ═══

**You do not guess the number of layers.**
1. **COGNITIVE LIMIT / SPAN OF CONTROL — 3 to 7 children per parent.** Twenty components under one subsystem cannot have their interfaces managed by a human. Add a layer.
2. **INDEPENDENT LIFECYCLES** — a part with its own upgrade cycle, testing process or supplier belongs in its own layer.
3. **CONWAY'S LAW** — layers tend to match team structure; three engineering teams usually means three main subsystems.
4. **STOP** when going deeper adds no value for tracking requirements, managing risk, or assigning work.
Standard breakdown: SoS ▸ System ▸ Subsystem ▸ Component ▸ Part/Material.

⭐⭐ THE INVERSION, AND IT IS THE WHOLE IDEA: **SPAN OF CONTROL MAKES DEPTH A CONSEQUENCE, NOT A CHOICE.** If a parent may hold 3–7 children, then the number of layers a design NEEDS falls out of how many parts it has. Nobody declares it and nobody has to know a vocabulary. That is a third answer to the ladder question that neither the closed enum nor the open ladder considered: reflow2 could COMPUTE the depth a design requires and say so, instead of asking the user to name rungs.

═══ AND IT IS TESTABLE ON CONTAMINATED DATA, BECAUSE IT IS STRUCTURAL ═══

Span of control is a property of the graph, not a preference, so the contamination does not block it. MEASURED 2026-08-25, children per parent on the CONTAINS spine:

    design                 fan-out per parent          parents over 7
    flo2 (concept)         6, 2, 2, 1, 1               0  ✓
    qbench                 5, 3                        0  ✓
    dynograph-foundation   4, 4, 3, 2                  0  ✓
    dev_storyflow          18, 11, 1, 1                2  (worst: storyflow = 18)
    reflow2 (own)          28, 25, 13, 10, 6, 4, 2, 2  4  (worst: coherence-loop = 28)

⭐ THE SMALL, DELIBERATELY-SHAPED DESIGNS ALREADY OBEY THE RULE WITHOUT BEING TOLD. flo2, qbench and dynograph-foundation are inside 3–7 everywhere. The two that violate it are the two grown by accretion over months — and **reflow2's OWN design is the worst offender in the sample, at 28 children under `sys:coherence-loop`, four times the limit.** That is a good reason to keep using it as a litmus test and a bad reason to treat it as an exemplar.

⭐ IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE FLATNESS FOUND EARLIER WITHOUT NEEDING A PREFERENCE. dev_storyflow has 84–101 components with ZERO nesting; the earlier reading was "users do not need depth". Under this doctrine that is not a preference, it is a **defect with a number attached**: 101 children under one Project is 14x the upper bound, and the design needs roughly two more layers. The rule turns a shrug into a finding.

═══ WHAT REFLOW2 COULD DO WITH IT ═══

- **A `span_of_control` detector.** Cheap, deterministic, and it fires on the graph reflow2 already has. NOT already built: `evaluate_allocation`'s `god_components` looks for ARTICULATION POINTS in the capability-coupling graph — a different axis entirely, and it would not have caught any of the five rows above.
- **A derived answer to "how many layers do I need?"** — computed from part count and fan-out, offered rather than demanded.
- ⚠️ AND THE HONEST OBJECTION, recorded beside it: 3–7 is a HUMAN cognitive bound, and reflow2's stated posture is `dec:report-dont-judge`. Shipping 7 as a threshold would embed a rule of thumb as if it were a law, which is exactly the over-modelling this project refuses elsewhere. Reporting the FAN-OUT and letting the reader judge is the version that survives that objection; a hard threshold is the version that does not.
- Rules 2 and 3 are NOT computable from the graph today. Independent lifecycles would need release/supplier data reflow2 does not hold, and Conway's Law would need team structure — `OWNED_BY` exists and could carry it, which is the nearest hook.

═══ THE EVIDENCE THAT WOULD ACTUALLY SETTLE IT ═══

Real-world case studies rather than this workshop's own output. Candidates, none pursued: published INCOSE/NASA systems-engineering case studies with documented WBS depth; open architecture documents (an aircraft, a spacecraft bus, a telescope control system); and the one closest to hand — **NSLS-II's bluesky stack, which Anthony works on and which is a real ~10-year-old system nobody at this workshop designed.** That last one is the only sample available that is both real and uncontaminated by reflow2.
properties.name: OPEN — span of control (3–7 children per parent) makes the NUMBER OF LAYERS a computed consequence rather than a declared choice; and every design measured so far predates reflow2 having rungs at all
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

Kept separate from `dec:idea-is-a-declared-rung-name-the-right-shape-for-decomposition-depth` (which compares five carriers for depth, all of which DECLARE it) and from `dec:the-decomposition-ladder-is-open-not-a-fixed-enum` (which decided the ladder opens). This proposes that depth need not be declared at all — that span of control makes the number of layers a computed consequence of part count. That is a different kind of answer from any of the five shapes, which is why it is its own node rather than a sixth bullet on that one.

It also carries Anthony's correction to the evidence base, which invalidates a conclusion drawn earlier today from the same measurements.
